title: Genistein suppresses renal fibrosis in chronic kidney disease through regulation of the CCAR2/SIRT1/p53 signaling axis.
authors: Li, Tong; Bai, Qiu-Xiang; Luo, Kang-Meng; Jia, Jian; Wang, Li; Tan, Rui-Zhi
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究金雀异黄酮通过CCAR2/SIRT1/p53信号轴抑制肾纤维化，核心是药物-蛋白互作与信号通路，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与课题无关。
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD), a major global health burden, is characterized by progressive renal fibrosis, for which effective therapies are lacking. While the natural isoflavone genistein (Gen) has been documented to possess broad anti-fibrotic properties, its specific function and underlying mechanism in renal fibrosis remain largely undefined. In this study, we demonstrate that Gen administration significantly attenuates renal fibrosis in both UUO and adenine-induced murine CKD models. To elucidate the molecular mechanism, we employed a strategy using biotin-conjugated Gen as a bait for pull-down assays, followed by mass spectrometry analysis, which successfully identified CCAR2 as a novel direct cellular target of Gen. This specific interaction was further validated by CETSA, molecular docking and Co-IP, which confirmed the binding site at 108 Tryptophan. Functional investigations revealed that CCAR2 intrinsically functions as a promoter of renal fibrogenesis, and its overexpression exacerbated the fibrotic response, whereas its genetic knockdown or pharmacological inhibition by Gen potently alleviated fibrosis in vitro and in vivo settings. Mechanistically, our data indicate that CCAR2 acts as an endogenous inhibitor of SIRT1 deacetylase activity, consequently leading to increased acetylation and transcriptional activation of the downstream effector p53. Critically, genistein, by directly binding to CCAR2, sterically relieves its inhibitory effect on SIRT1, thereby restoring SIRT1 activity and subsequently suppressing p53-mediated pro-fibrotic signaling, ultimately conferring robust protection against renal fibrosis. Collectively, our findings reveal that genistein ameliorates renal fibrosis through precise targeting of the newly identified CCAR2/SIRT1/p53 signaling pathway, thereby offering a promising therapeutic strategy for patients with fibrotic CKD.
abstract_zh: 慢性肾脏病（CKD）作为一项重大全球健康负担，以进行性肾纤维化为特征，目前缺乏有效疗法。尽管天然异黄酮染料木素（Gen）已被记载具有广泛的抗纤维化特性，但其在肾纤维化中的具体功能及潜在机制仍 largely 未明确。在本研究中，我们证明Gen给药在UUO和腺嘌呤诱导的小鼠CKD模型中显著减轻肾纤维化。为阐明分子机制，我们采用生物素标记的Gen作为诱饵进行pull-down实验，随后结合质谱分析，成功鉴定出CCAR2为Gen的新型直接细胞靶点。该特异性相互作用通过CETSA、分子对接和Co-IP进一步验证，并确认结合位点为108位色氨酸。功能研究表明，CCAR2本质上作为肾纤维化发生的促进因子，其过表达加剧纤维化反应，而其基因敲低或Gen的药理抑制在体外和体内环境中均有效缓解纤维化。机制上，我们的数据表明CCAR2作为SIRT1去乙酰化酶活性的内源性抑制剂，从而导致下游效应因子p53的乙酰化增加及转录激活。关键的是，染料木素通过直接结合CCAR2，空间上解除其对SIRT1的抑制作用，从而恢复SIRT1活性，并随后抑制p53介导的促纤维化信号，最终赋予对肾纤维化的强效保护。综上，我们的发现揭示染料木素通过精准靶向新鉴定的CCAR2/SIRT1/p53信号通路改善肾纤维化，从而为纤维化CKD患者提供一种有前景的治疗策略。
